title: Check yourself: Plans, partial results, coverage notes and the practice

questions.stem: Scenario S3, multi-agent research system. A subagent returns an empty list when its lookup service times out, and the coordinator's report says that the topic has nothing in the sources. What fixes the cause?

options.text: Treat every blank answer as a failure and send it back for another attempt
options.says: Ruled out because "Treat the empty result as a failure, and the system retries a search that already worked".

options.text: Mark the timeout as a typed failure, distinct from a genuine absence of matches
options.says: A failure and a valid empty result are different values with different handling.

options.text: Remove the topics with no results from the report so that no false claim remains in it
options.says: Ruled out because "A report that quietly omits a topic is saying something false by leaving it out".

options.text: Have the coordinator rerun any topic whose report says that nothing was found
options.says: Ruled out because "A search that runs and finds nothing has succeeded", so rerunning it repeats a finished job and leaves the timeout unreported.

origin.section: One decision per result, and the run goes on

questions.stem: Scenario S3, multi-agent research system. A synthesis step merges findings on six topics. Two sources were unreachable, and one search found nothing. The report reads as a complete survey. What should the step add?

options.text: A confidence score for the whole report, shown as a single number between zero and one
options.says: Ruled out because the note is "the place where the system's own plan is compared with what happened", and a single score compares nothing.

options.text: A line saying that some sources may be unavailable at the moment of writing
options.says: Ruled out because a line like that "names no topic and no cause, so no reader can act on it".

options.text: A note that sorts subjects into evidenced and unevidenced, with the cause of each gap
options.says: The note compares what was planned with what happened, topic by topic.

options.text: A longer introduction describing in detail how the survey was carried out and by whom
options.says: Ruled out because "A reader who sees a confident survey with a hole in it learns about the hole later and from someone else".
